top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a distinct invention: the magic-wavelength condition cancels the trapping light shift so many neutral atoms are interrogated at once, unlike the comb (2005) or single-ion control (2012). It has been reproduced and compared across independent laboratories near 1e-18 and already underpins geodesy, constants tests and the preparation of the redefinition of the second. The Katori (concept and first realisation) and Ye (record accuracy, many-body regime) allocation maps onto two necessary contributions, and the citation can be scoped to the lattice clock itself. No award would withhold a mature, well-attributed achievement.
recusal_note: Possible professional proximity as an atomic physicist and quantum-optics researcher to the optical-clock field, including laser spectroscopy and Lund colleagues; no specific connection to Katori or Ye apparent from profile.
